PLANTING_PLAN.status: Eighteen spring 2027 trees are ordered and not planted yet: Cummins 039970, Roots to Fruits RTF12645, Raintree U2TM4QUWD, and Trees of Antiquity 2R8PX8Q8P. Roots to Fruits is confirmed, but $666 is still due. Eighteen trees are still to buy, and nothing is grafted yet
PLANTING_PLAN.summary: Chosen in October 2026 for a short-season, frost-prone U-pick orchard at about 4,750 ft (the frost dates are on the site climate page). Disease-resistant apples that ripen early or in mid-season fill R4 to R6 and the grafted row R1; hardy tart and sweet cherries and a Seckel pear fill R8 to R10; and the shared stone-fruit rows R11 and R12 get four plums, two apricots, and four peaches, three of the peaches replacing ones that died in their pots. R13 to R15 stay open for later.
PLANTING_PLAN.rootstock_advice: Ask nurseries for semi-dwarf trees (about 60 to 75 percent of standard; G.890, G.214 or M.7 for apples). The grid is 18 x 20 ft and the site is dry and windy, so dwarf stocks (M.27, M.9, B.9) would need permanent stakes and leave gaps.
PLANTING_PLAN.graft_advice: The 13 grafts in R1 go onto rootstocks you already own: 11 M-111 (vigorous, semi-standard), 2 EMLA 7 (semi-dwarf) and 1 of unknown type, so one rootstock is left as a spare. Order scionwood in winter from a nursery that sells it for spring 2027 (some sell out early), keep it cold and damp until grafting, and graft in early spring as the rootstock buds begin to swell. Use the two EMLA 7 rootstocks for Redfree, a vigorous scion (its third tree goes on an M-111), and put lower-vigor scions such as Pixie Crunch on the vigorous M-111. Grafted trees take longer to bear than bought trees. Check that a cultivar may be propagated at home before ordering scionwood.
PLANTING_PLAN.shipping_note: Confirm that each nursery ships the item to Idaho before ordering; some retailers exclude Idaho for some items. Cummins Nursery accepted the apple order below for Idaho and charged a phytosanitary certificate, but its checkout will not send peach, plum, cherry, nectarine, or apricot trees, scion, or rootstock there. Roots to Fruits, Raintree Nursery, and Trees of Antiquity each accepted an Idaho order on October 27, 2026. That acceptance is for those orders only.
